photos.c: Early leaders in the Championship 5 3/4. New member Oliver Foote (52) follows Alister Horton (49) who shields second place man David North.
Above Left; Oliver Foote on his way to winning the Surrey 10,000m Championships. He followed this with a silver in the Surrey 5000m and headed our Rankings over 5000m for 1983.

West side story. 1 mile into the 5¾ and the field is bunched waiting for the break. Following Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin are Bob Lettin(71), Leo Coy, Olly Foote, Laurie O'Hara, Mike Nouch,Eric Crutcher(70),Martin Lake,Simon Williamson(68),and Keith Sinclair(22).

Oliver Foote hit a purple patch in Autumn -after holidaying with the Motes and Gilbeys- and in the Yacht '3' not only became the second fastest man round the course but also became the first to win from scratch.

Back Cover.   The South of Thames Junior C.C.Championship provided a unique and exciting spectacle for Belgrave supporters when at the 2 mile mark our men held the first 4 places in the 300 strong field. Our picture shows eventual winner Oliver Foote in the lead from Mark Sinclair(6th), John Gladwin(2nd), and Dave North(7th), the team's winning score being the best ever recorded in the 50 year history of this race - a fitting result with Gordon Biscoe as the S.O.T. President.

Into the bell in the 1500m and they've shed the pacemaker, Stu' Paton (entry fee sponsored by Oliver Foote to set up a sub 4!) Mark Sinclair looks a picture of relaxation and goes on to a sixth successive win. The next three hung on for pb's - Olly, Frank Ward (behind Mark) and John Booth in his seasonal debut after injury!

Gary Staines, fresh from his Olympic 5000m final spearheaded a fine Belgrave team effort in the first Surrey C.C.League Match. Gary (21), Jean Paul Wright (8), followed by Mark Sinclair, Matthew Stickles, Mike Hayes (20), Francis Ward, Marcello Bizio (15) and Ollie Foote (11).

Oliver Foote has had one of his best ever points score for our British and achieved a long held ambition to win the Surrey 5000m title to add to the 10000m wins achieved several years ago. Here he leads a classy Div.1 BAL field with Andrew Lloyd just behind him .
Ollie Foote, on his way to 3rd place in the GRE final at Gateshead [a].

Above: Top left to right - Ollie Foote, second Belgravian home at Coulsdon, a hirsute Frank Ward (we hear he has taken it off for his wedding) and Marco Mazzotta., who has steadily improved since last Autumn. Bottom - Jon Hobbs, Andy Paton and Don Anderson, the man who runs the Club '10' and then goes round again to collect the flags (and probably went round before to set them up!

Opposite page: The "last" Belgrave-Southern Relay.
Top. High noon and the starter sends 61 runners off on the first leg. Jon Hobbs completes his lap of the "top" and nears the crowd at the Hand in Hand.
Centre. Ollie Foote sends Marcello Bizio away on the last stage. Jim Estall loosens up for the London Marathon with a 25:53 long leg. Second fastest long stage of the day and another mark in the all-time top 20 - Paul Evans has an easy run!
Bottom. Jim Estall launches Marco Mazzotta. Frank Ward reaches the summit of Wool Road. Putting on a good show for visiting relations, "Aussie" Brandon Reid streaks off the Common for a nippy second leg.
